Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: production 2D side-view 24x24 pixel-art biome TILESET ATLAS. Reference images are STYLE REFERENCES ONLY: existing Tervain game tiles enlarged with labels. Match their chunky low-resolution pixel clusters, subdued 6-10-color material palettes, moderate contrast and simple readable silhouettes, NOT painterly or high-resolution detail. No labels or text in output.
Create one perfectly regular atlas: EXACTLY FOUR columns and THREE rows of square cells, full canvas 4:3 aspect ratio, ideally 1536x1152. ZERO gutters, ZERO margins, ZERO frames, no shadows around cells. Each cell is exactly a 24x24 logical pixel tile enlarged 16 times with nearest-neighbor: big square hard pixels, absolutely no antialiasing. All 12 cells must align precisely to the regular grid and completely fill it. ROWS 1 AND 2 are edge-to-edge opaque square repeating material tiles, no isolated block outlines, no lighting bevels or borders. In row1 col1 only include a thin surface cap at the TOP; all other opaque terrain tiles fill all edges. Row2 col1-2 are distinctly dim, quiet background walls, NOT black; col3-4 liquid body and liquid surface. ROW3 contains FOUR separate cutout decorations, each on REAL TRANSPARENT alpha with no background or checkerboard, centered horizontally, contained inside its cell leaving 2 logical pixels of empty space at left and right. Upright decorations root at bottom y=22; hanging decorations attach at top y=1. No decoration overlaps cells. All drawings front/side orthographic, no perspective, no UI, no characters, no scenes, no words, no tile numbers. This is actual game asset art rather than an illustration of a tileset.
